clue.text: Bat, net & lines set out for the game

indicators.note: to set out is to lay out or arrange, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Equipment for a sport is being laid out ready to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' tells you to rearrange BAT, NET and LINES; the ampersand and 'for' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ping-pong is a game played with bats over a net on a table.

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail or welcome
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A head of state greets the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to assert or declare it, a close synonym.

indicators.note: possibly suggests a different version of the word enlists, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who pays attention might also join up.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend to someone is to heed or hear them out.

clue.text: Sailor on northern stretch of water

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A seaman sails on a lake in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: A tarn is a small mountain lake, a word common in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mountain lake is a body of water.

indicators.note: putting the letters of seems in into a new order means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Punishment for wrongdoing seems quite fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' reads as 'appropriate', but 'in' is part of the fodder and 'order' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis was the Greek goddess of vengeance, so the word means just punishment.

parts.note: barristers belong to the ... of Court in London, and a refresher is both an extra fee paid to counsel and a drink, served in a pub

explanation.surface: Lawyers collect further fees somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'refresher' is a fee paid to a barrister for a long case; the other sense is a drink, so pubs fit too.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers join one of the Inns of Court, and pubs serve drinks too.

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as a ..., a fishmonger's booth

explanation.surface: A market stall has been booked to sell fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool, aloof person is distant; split up, the word describes a counter selling fish.

parts.note: not audio tape but a tape measure: what you record when you use one

explanation.surface: Someone is making a recording on magnetic tape.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading a tape measure gives you a size or dimension.

clue.text: They are better than they make themselves out to be

definitions.text: They are better than they make themselves out to be

parts.words: They are better than they make themselves out to be
parts.note: 'better' in the sense of healthier: people faking illness to avoid work

explanation.surface: Modest people underrate their own abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Shirkers pretend to be sick when actually healthier than they claim.

clue.text: It may be taken as an indication of health

definitions.text: It may be taken as an indication of health

parts.words: It may be taken as an indication of health
parts.note: 'taken' as a doctor takes a reading with a thermometer

explanation.surface: Something is regarded as a sign of wellbeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor takes a patient's body heat reading to check for fever.

clue.text: Ably matched, perhaps, in ambitious Shakespearean role

indicators.note: perhaps hints that a rearranged version of ably matched is wanted

explanation.surface: An actor well suited to playing a scheming Shakespeare character.
explanation.definitionFit: The wife in the Scottish play drives her husband to murder for the crown out of ambition.

indicators.note: the potential in star is what its letters could become when rearranged

explanation.surface: A monarch with the makings of a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was used by the emperors of Russia.

parts.note: jelly or concrete sets when it stiffens

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a hair stand stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: A seta is a biological term for a stiff hair or bristle, as on a worm.
explanation.definitionFit: In zoology and botany the word names a stiff hair-like structure.

parts.note: literally hammering a pointed metal spike into wood, as well as making an argument stick

explanation.surface: Someone is emphasising an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammering a spike in is literally driving its point home; figuratively, it means pinning something down.

clue.text: Yields to pressure and hands over

explanation.surface: Someone caves in and surrenders the goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress bends under weight; a donor presents a present.

parts.note: 'well-earned' split as earned while well, that is wages received while ill

explanation.surface: Ill-gotten or undeserved cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Wages paid while an employee is off ill are earned while unwell.

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new form, so the letters of brush are rearranged

explanation.surface: New scrub springs up in the woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush is a woody plant forming part of the low growth beneath trees.

clue.text: Expresses regret for glue that's weak, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: size is a thin, weak glue or sealant used on paper and plaster

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for adhesive that doesn't hold.
explanation.walkthrough: Size is a thin gelatinous wash used to seal plaster or stiffen paper; 'we hear' turns it into a near-identical sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathing out audibly shows sorrow or disappointment.

clue.text: Boozy group return to hold a wild party

indicators.note: return says the letters held there are read backwards
to hold says the words Boozy group contain the wanted letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gang of drinkers come back to throw a riotous party.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left the hidden word without a signal; 'to hold' is it, so the definition is 'a wild party', not 'hold a wild party'. 'return' turns YGRO, held across 'Boozy group', round.
explanation.definitionFit: A debauched revel is a wild party, so the noun phrase works as a whole.

definitions.meaning: a sunken courtyard in front of a basement, in British houses
an extent of surface measured in square units

explanation.surface: Asking whether a unit is linear or squared.
explanation.walkthrough: In British homes the paved yard in front of a basement is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a courtyard space and the size of a surface share the word.

definitions.meaning: read literally, to release pressing down by allowing it to rise

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stop pressing down so hard.
explanation.definitionFit: To slacken is to relax; literally, releasing pressure lets it rise.

parts.note: 'left' means bequeathed in a will, not remaining

explanation.surface: Someone receives the leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: A beneficiary receives what someone bequeaths in a will.

clue.text: He foresees a hold-up over the reform

parts.note: a prop is a support that holds something up

indicators.note: reform means re-form, so the letters of the word the are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone predicts a delay to the reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places PROP above HET (the rearrangement of THE) in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer predicts the future.

clue.text: Goes looking for a scrap when surrounded by enemies

indicators.note: something surrounded by something else sits inside it

parts.note: foes are enemies
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Someone hunts for a fight while hemmed in by foes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight, but here it is a piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To scavenge is to search about for food or supplies.

clue.text: One never knows what it may hold for the present

definitions.text: One never knows what it may hold for the present

parts.words: One never knows what it may hold for the present
parts.note: 'the present' sounds like now, but it is a gift hidden in a lucky dip at a British fair

explanation.surface: A remark on the unpredictability of current events.
explanation.walkthrough: A British lucky dip: a tub of bran with wrapped gifts hidden in it, at fêtes and parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky dip tub hides small gifts buried in husks, so you never know what you will pull out.

clue.text: One bound on a crest of a wave, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells you a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: surf is the foam on breaking waves

explanation.surface: Someone leaps onto the top of a breaking wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' suggests a jump, but it means tied to the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval peasant was tied to his lord's land.

clue.text: Left in charge but desert one's post

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

explanation.surface: An official left in charge abandons the job anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left in charge' reads as a phrase, but it is L inside FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Running away is abandoning one's position.

clue.text: Settles in the country in T France

definitions.meaning: the French word for nation or countryside

explanation.surface: Someone takes up residence in rural France.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing a debt means paying it; the French for land is the same word.

definitions.meaning: poultry swallow small stones to grind food in the gizzard

explanation.surface: Cowards need bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chickens' looks like cowards, but means actual hens who peck tiny stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluck is determination; hens eat small stones to digest food.

definitions.note: a verb phrase for the noun: an insect that has a bite

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour

explanation.surface: A flavour that grows stronger has a sharp kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has bite' seems to describe a flavour, but it describes a small biting fly.
explanation.definitionFit: This midge-like insect bites, so it has a bite.

clue.text: Slam the coin frantically into it!

definitions.text: Slam the coin frantically into it!

indicators.note: frantically suggests wild movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A frustrated gambler bangs money into a fruit machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A coin-operated gambling device is where you feed money.

indicators.note: shifting means moving the letters of scene around
break means the letters of it's tea are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Does changing the stage set call for a pause for a cuppa?
explanation.walkthrough: 'scene-shifting' and 'tea-break' look like compound nouns, but each hyphen joins fodder to its indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand or make unavoidable is the meaning of both words.
